questions.question: What are the (part 91) maintenance requirements for an emergency locator transmitter (ELT)?
questions.idealAnswer: An ELT must be inspected within in 12 months of the previous inspection. The inspection includes; proper installation, battery corrosion, battery life, operation of controls and the crash sensor, and the presence of a sufficient signal at the antenna.

questions.question: What are the record keeping requirements for a (part 91) Emergency locator(ELT)?
questions.idealAnswer: A record of inspection of an ELT must be recorded in the aircraft log book including the expiration date of the battery. This also must be recorded on the outside of the ELT.

questions.question: Name some concerns when inspecting coaxial cable installations on aircraft.
questions.idealAnswer: Some coax cable used on pulse-type transceivers must be a specific length. Attachment of cable ends must be secure. Coaxial cable should be secured along its entire run at intervals of approximately two feet. Proper impedance must exist.

questions.question: What are the requirements of routing coaxial cable?
questions.idealAnswer: Coax cable should be secured to the aircraft structure approximately every two feet. It should not be tied to or routed with another wire bundle. questions.question: What is the means of identification of commonly used communication and or navigation antennas?
questions.idealAnswer: The shape and length of an antenna can sometimes be used to reason what type of antenna is under consideration. The orientation or polarization and location on the aircraft can also give clues. The three basic types of antennas are: the dipole, the Marconi, and the loop. Dipole antennas, often used for VOR frequencies, may have a “V” shape. They are commonly located at the empennage or mounted on the underside of the fuselage. The “V” shape indicates its horizontal polarization that makes the antennas good at receiving signals that are not coming head on. The Marconi antenna is simply a straight conductor. It uses the skin or on fabric aircraft, conductive material under the skin, to form a conductor of 2 wavelength of the signals it is designed to receive or transmit. The Marconi antenna is vertically polarized and creates a field that is omnidirectional. VHF communication radios can use this type of antenna. The conductor in a loop antenna forms a loop. Having a loop shape to receive radio signals significantly affects the field characteristics of the antenna. It is highly sensitive to the direction from which the signal is received. Loop antennas are used extensively in navigation such as for an ADF radio. Often the loop antennas are enclosed in a housing broad enough to conceal the entire antenna which is frequently mounted on the underside of the fuselage.

questions.question: Describe the function and operation for a static discharger.
questions.idealAnswer: Static dischargers, or wicks, are installed on aircraft to reduce radio interference. The interference is caused by a corona discharge emitted from the aircraft as a result of precipitation static. Corona occurs in short pulses that produce noise at the radio frequency spectrum. Static dischargers are normally mounted on the trailing edge of control surfaces, wing tips, and the vertical stabilizer. They discharge precipitation static at points a critical distance away from avionics antennas where there is little or no coupling of the static to cause interference or noise.
